paragraphs: Marbim bitpillot vetachanunim behoshana rabba, ki hu siyyum n" yom shennatenu leyisrael bechesed elyon laasot bahem teshuba vetitqabbel teshubatam, vehem sheloshim deelul miyyom rishon shel r"ch vk" yom detishre remez laddabar en na ella leshon baqqasha lekak natenu n" yom letzorek habbaqqashot vetachanunim veyom zeh hu siyyum yom n", velaken niqra hvshn" raba kelomar hoshea et yom n" shehu rabba dehakkol holek achar hechatum:

clarification.explanation: One increases prayers and supplications on Hoshana Rabbah, since this day is the conclusion of the fifty-one days that were given to Israel through supreme kindness in order to do teshuvah in them — thirty days of Elul (from Rosh Chodesh) and twenty-one days of Tishrei (until Hoshana Rabbah). The hint: the word "na" expresses a request, and so these fifty-one (na) days were given especially for requests and supplications, and the day of Hoshana Rabbah is the conclusion of those fifty-one days. From this comes its name — "Hoshana Rabbah," meaning "save, please, the fifty-first day, which is great" — for everything follows the final seal.
takeaways: Hoshana Rabbah is the conclusion of the fifty-one days of teshuvah (thirty in Elul, twenty-one in Tishrei), and so one increases prayers and supplications on it as the close of the season of requests.

paragraphs: Belel hv"r beet chatzot layla nigmar venaasa bechinat chotam hachitzon lemala, ki byvh"k nigmar chotam happenimi shehu haiqqar yoter, velaken bhv"r nimsarin happitqin, v"p shennimseru happitqin yesh od zeman lehatztzala ad yom ch' atzeret, velaken tzarik lehitorer bitshuba gedola bhv"r veyihyeh libbo chared bitshuba kol hayyom kullo:

clarification.explanation: On the night of Hoshana Rabbah, at midnight, an outer seal is completed and made above — whereas on Yom Kippur the inner seal, which is the more essential one, was completed. Therefore on Hoshana Rabbah the "notes" (the verdicts of judgment) are handed over, but even though they have already been handed over, there is still time for rescue until the day of Shemini Atzeret. One must therefore be aroused to great teshuvah on Hoshana Rabbah, and a person's heart should tremble in teshuvah the whole day.
takeaways: On the night of Hoshana Rabbah an "outer seal" is sealed (as opposed to the inner seal, completed on Yom Kippur), but there is still time to correct matters until Shemini Atzeret — hence one must be aroused to great teshuvah that day.

paragraphs: Yilmod seder hamtuqqan besimcha ubehitlahabut ki belimmud seper mishneh tora naaseh iqqar hattiqqun harauy lihyot beyom zeh, umeat qodem chatzot layla yomru q"sh sheal hammitta im happesuqim sheyyesh immah, veachar chatzot layla yomar birkot hashshachar, veraq birkat hattora lo yomar ella ad achar ammud hashshachar:

clarification.explanation: On the night of Hoshana Rabbah one should study the established tikkun (the tikkun for the night of Hoshana Rabbah) with joy and enthusiasm, because through the study of the Book of Mishneh Torah (Devarim) the essential rectification appropriate to this day is accomplished. Shortly before midnight one recites the Shema said upon retiring, with its accompanying verses, and after midnight one recites the morning blessings — except for the blessing on the Torah, which should be recited only after dawn.
takeaways: On the night of Hoshana Rabbah one studies a special tikkun (centered mainly on the Book of Devarim); before midnight one recites the bedtime Shema, and after midnight the morning blessings — except for the blessing on the Torah, which is delayed until dawn.

paragraphs: Yitpallelu shacharit umusap bekavvana vehitlahabut, ki millebad hachiyyub sheyyesh bazeh mikkoach qedushshat hayyom od tzarik lehitpallel behitlahabut kede shello tigbar alayv hashshena veyabo lide kamma teiyyot battepilla ubirkoteha ulekamma chesronot meachar shehaya neor kol hallayla, gam tzarik ledaqdeq heteb shello yitu beor hallebana veyitpallu qodem ammud hashshachar, deyadua bizman mahari"l za"l tau bekak vegazar mahari"l za"l al hatztzibbur taanit g' yamim baabur zot:

clarification.explanation: One must pray Shacharit and Musaf on Hoshana Rabbah with intent and enthusiasm — both because of the sanctity of the day, and so that the fatigue from having studied all night does not overtake him and cause errors in the prayer and its blessings, and deficiencies from having been awake the whole night. One must be especially careful not to mistake the light of the moon [for dawn] and pray before dawn by mistake — in the time of the Maharil, of blessed memory, the community erred in this, and as a penalty he decreed upon the community a three-day fast.
takeaways: One must pray Shacharit and Musaf on Hoshana Rabbah with enthusiasm, and must be especially careful not to mistake moonlight for dawn and actually pray before dawn.

paragraphs: En regilin laasot melaka shel chol beyom hv"r ad achar yetziatam mibbet hakkeneset veyesh mesirin apillu hakkis shel hammaot mecheqam, mihu im darko litten tzedaqa laaniyyim bebet hakkeneset vegam g' perutot bappasuq veatta moshel bekol asher bipsuqim vibarek david, lo yebattel mitzot yeqarot ellu bishbil chasidut zo:

clarification.explanation: It is not customary to do weekday labor on the day of Hoshana Rabbah until after leaving the synagogue, and some even remove the money pouch from their bosom (so as not to appear to be handling weekday items). Nevertheless, one whose practice is to give charity to the poor in the synagogue, and also three coins at the verse "and You rule over all" within the verses "And David blessed" (as mentioned in earlier halachot), should not give up these precious mitzvot on account of that same piety of removing the money pouch.
takeaways: One should not engage in weekday labor on Hoshana Rabbah until leaving the synagogue, but one should not forgo, on that account, the mitzvah of giving charity in the synagogue.

paragraphs: Achar shenniknesu kol hachasadim beyom zeh "y sukka velulab veshiba haqqapot, az niknasim hachamishsha geburot achar qaddish titqabbel, veellu hachamishsha geburot niknasim "y chabatat chamishsha baddim shel araba, al ken achar qaddish titqabbel shel seder z' haqqapot yiqqach kol adam chamishsha baddim shel araba sheyyihyu kesherim kedin araba shebballulab, veyachabot chamishsha peamim al haqqarqa, vikavven bachabatot ellu kede latet bibchinat he" acharona shebbeshem hvy"h b"h shehi sod hammalkut chamishsha geburot mntzp"k, vikavven bekol chabata beot echad dmntzp"k kepi seder zeh velo keseder kmnp"tz:

clarification.explanation: After all five aspects of "chesed" have entered on the day of Hoshana Rabbah (through the sukkah, the lulav, and the seven hakafot), the five "gevurot" enter after the Kaddish Titkabel — and this is done through the beating of five willow branches. Therefore, after the Kaddish Titkabel at the conclusion of the seven hakafot, each person takes five valid willow branches (valid according to the law of the willow of the lulav) and beats them five times on the ground, with the intention of drawing, into the final heh of the Name Havayah (the secret of Malchut), the five gevurot alluded to in the final-form letters mem-nun-tzadi-peh-chaf — intending with each beating one of these letters, in the order mem-nun-tzadi-peh-chaf and not in any other order.
takeaways: The beating of the five willow branches on Hoshana Rabbah (after Kaddish Titkabel, at the conclusion of the seven hakafot) is mystically intended to draw the five gevurot (the final-form letters mem-nun-tzadi-peh-chaf) into Malchut.

paragraphs: Yiqshor chamishsha baddim ellu beyachad, veyachabot bahem bekoach al haqqarqa, velo tihyeh merutztzepet baabanim o beetzim, deqarqa tzarik bedabar zeh, veyachabot bahem bekoach, v"p shekkatab bas' bikkure yaaqob detob lechakkot ad sheyyasir healin, la modena bazeh ki rauy sheyyihyu habbaddim bekashrutam ushelemutam bekol hachabatot kullam:

clarification.explanation: One should bind the five willow branches together and beat them forcefully on the ground (not on a floor paved with stones or wood — actual earth is required). There is an opinion (in the book Bikurei Yaakov) that it is good to continue striking until the leaves fall off by themselves from the force of the beating, but the Ben Ish Chai disagrees with this, since it is proper that the branches remain valid and whole throughout all the beatings (rather than intending to shake off the leaves through the beatings).
takeaways: One beats the five willow branches, bound together, on actual ground (not a paved floor), with force, taking care that the branches remain whole with their leaves throughout all the beatings — one does not continue striking specifically in order to shake off the leaves.

paragraphs: Araba zo dinah kaaraba shebballulab sheen lipsoa aleha velo lezalzel bah, uminhagenu lehatznia araba zo ad happesach lisrop bah et hechametz, vehallulab yisrepu oto betannur shemmassiqin beereb pesach lematztzat mitzva:

clarification.explanation: The law of the willow used for the beating is the same as the law of the willow of the lulav — one may not step on it and must not treat it with disrespect. The custom is to store this willow away until Pesach, and to burn the chametz with it; the lulav, on the other hand, is burned in the oven that is heated on the eve of Pesach for the sake of baking the matzah of the mitzvah.
takeaways: The willow used for the beating is set aside for burning the chametz at Pesach (not discarded disrespectfully), while the lulav is burned in the matzah oven on the eve of Pesach.

paragraphs: Yesh liqrot beyom hv"r nebuat chaggay si' b' bashshebii beesrim veechad lachodesh veku' ad etten shalom neum Adonai tzebaot vehem t' pesuqim km"sh rab yaabe"tz za"l, gam qorin beyom hv"r bihoshua si' v, vesabbotem et hair kol anshe hammilchama veku', ad vayyomer yehoshua el haam hariu ki natan Adonai lakem et hair, veyadua m"sh birushalmi beha sheshshaninu al hv"r shehayu maqqipin hammizbeach sheba peamim shehu zeker lannes hannizkar biricho "sh, ubeemet kol ish bilbabo yabin ki sod haqqapot ellu shehem shesh vesheba, haqqapot ellu hakkol oleh beqaneh echad al ken dabar beitto mah tob:

clarification.explanation: On Hoshana Rabbah one reads the prophecy of Chaggai, chapter 2, from the verse "in the seventh month, on the twenty-first of the month" until "I will grant peace, says the Lord of Hosts" — nine verses, as Rav Yaavetz wrote. One also reads on this day from Joshua chapter 6, the story of the war of Jericho — "and you shall go around the city, all the men of war" until "shout, for the Lord has given you the city." The Yerushalmi states that on Hoshana Rabbah they used to circle the altar seven times, in memory of the miracle of Jericho (where they circled the city seven times). The Ben Ish Chai notes that anyone will understand in his heart that the secret of the hakafot (six and seven) is entirely of one piece with this meaning — and this is a matter written in its proper time.
takeaways: On Hoshana Rabbah one reads the prophecy of Chaggai (concerning the building of the Second Temple) and the account of the fall of Jericho, since the seven hakafot of this day recall the seven circuits around Jericho.

paragraphs: Etrog shel lulab bashshebii asur leakelo, velibne eretz yisrael muttar beyom shemini atzeret, abal libne chu"l asur bashshemini atzeret umuttar besimchat tora shehu yom tob sheni, veim chal shemini atzeret beshabbat yesh oserin haetrog libne chu"l gam batteshii shehu achar hashshabbat:

clarification.explanation: The etrog of the lulav is forbidden to eat on the seventh day (Hoshana Rabbah). Residents of the Land of Israel may eat it already on Shemini Atzeret, but residents of the Diaspora are forbidden to eat it on Shemini Atzeret and may eat it only on Simchat Torah (the second festival day). If Shemini Atzeret falls on Shabbat, some forbid the etrog to residents of the Diaspora also on the ninth day, which follows Shabbat.
takeaways: The etrog is forbidden to eat on the seventh day (Hoshana Rabbah) for everyone; in the Land of Israel it is permitted from Shemini Atzeret, and in the Diaspora only from Simchat Torah (or later still, if Shemini Atzeret falls on Shabbat).

paragraphs: Sukka venoyah asurim libne chu"l lehanot mehem gam batteshii shehu yom sh"t, vehu haddin deasur letaltelam, veyizzaher kol yeme hammoed lebilti yiqqach min hassukka apillu qesam lachtzotz bo shinnayv ben mehassekak ben mehaddepanot vegam achar hammoed keshemmorid sukkato lo yipsa al atze hassukka ditshammeshi qedushsha hem, ak muttar lesarepam betannur, venahagu lehatzniam lehagala letzorek happesach:

clarification.explanation: The sukkah and its decorations are forbidden in benefit to residents of the Diaspora also on the ninth day (which is Simchat Torah for them), and the same law applies that it is forbidden to move them. Throughout the entire festival one must be careful not to take anything at all from the sukkah — even a small splinter to pick one's teeth — neither from the schach nor from the walls; and even after the festival, when one takes down the sukkah, one should not step on the sukkah's wood, since it served a sacred purpose. However, it is permitted to burn them in an oven, and the custom is to store them for use in the kashering process for Pesach.
takeaways: The sukkah and its decorations remain forbidden in benefit and in moving even on Simchat Torah for residents of the Diaspora; one may not step on the sukkah's wood after taking it down, though it may be burned or stored for kashering before Pesach.

paragraphs: Lel sh" omer battepilla et yom chag shemini atzeret hazzeh, veim taa veamar et chag hassukkot hazzeh chozer, veim nizkar shehu yom sh" veraq taa bilshono veamar chag hassukkot eno chozer:

clarification.explanation: On the night of Shemini Atzeret one says in the prayer, "this day of the festival of Shemini Atzeret." If he erred and said "this festival of Sukkot," he must repeat the prayer. But if in his heart he remembered that the day was Shemini Atzeret and only made a slip of the tongue, saying "the festival of Sukkot," he need not repeat it.
takeaways: A substantive error (thinking it is the festival of Sukkot) on the night of Shemini Atzeret requires repeating the prayer; a mere slip of the tongue (while knowing it is Shemini Atzeret) does not require repeating it.

paragraphs: En mebarekim bechu"l bsh" al hassukka, abal chayyabim lesheb bah velishon bah kishar yeme hechag veen lezalzel bazeh kelal, veraq tihyeh hayyeshiba belo beraka, umebarekin shehecheyanu belel sh" ubelel sh"t beqiddush hallayla, vetzarik layla vadday beqiddush bsh" bishbil birkat lesheb bassukka deyan mebarekin, ubesimchat tora bishbil yeshibat sukka deen yoshebin bah veokelin bachutz:

clarification.explanation: Residents of the Diaspora do not recite a blessing on Shemini Atzeret over sitting in the sukkah, but they are nonetheless obligated to sit and sleep in it as on the other days of the festival, and this must not be treated lightly at all — only the sitting itself is without a blessing. "Shehecheyanu" is recited both on the night of Shemini Atzeret (in the Kiddush) and on the night of Simchat Torah (in the Kiddush). The need for Shehecheyanu on the night of Shemini Atzeret stems from the fact that the blessing "to dwell in the sukkah" is not recited that evening, and on the night of Simchat Torah it stems from the fact that one does not sit in the sukkah at all that night, but eats outside.
takeaways: In the Diaspora one still sits in the sukkah on Shemini Atzeret without a blessing, and one recites Shehecheyanu at the night Kiddush of both Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah — to compensate for the absence of the blessing 'to dwell in the sukkah.'

paragraphs: Asur lehazkir hayyachid geshem bitpillat musap beyom sh" qodem sheyyakriz sh"tz, velaken hammitpallel yachid bebeto yamtin ad sheyyeda beberur shehikriz hsh"tz beezeh bet hakkeneset sheotah hair vekol adam sheshshakach veamar morid hattal velo amar morid haggeshem eno chozer:

clarification.explanation: It is forbidden for an individual to mention "rain" in the Musaf prayer of Shemini Atzeret before the prayer leader has announced it. Therefore, one praying individually at home should wait until he knows for certain that the prayer leader has made the announcement in some synagogue in that city. One who forgot and said "who causes the dew to descend" instead of "who causes the rain to descend" need not repeat the prayer.
takeaways: An individual should not mention 'He makes the wind blow and the rain descend' in the Musaf of Shemini Atzeret before the prayer leader has announced it in some synagogue in his city; a mistaken recitation ('who causes the dew to descend') does not require repeating the prayer.

paragraphs: Shenayim miqra veechad targum shel parashat vezot habberaka yiqraenna beyom hv"r velo beyom sh" mippene hattargum, veim shakach velo qeraah beyom hv"r yiqraenna beyom sh" achar mincha:

clarification.explanation: One should read "Sheniyim Mikra ve'Echad Targum" of the portion V'Zot HaBerachah on the day of Hoshana Rabbah, and not on Shemini Atzeret — because of the Aramaic translation (it is not customary to recite the Targum in the midst of Shemini Atzeret). If he forgot and did not read it on Hoshana Rabbah, he should read it on Shemini Atzeret after the Minchah prayer.
takeaways: The portion V'Zot HaBerachah (Sheniyim Mikra ve'Echad Targum) is read on Hoshana Rabbah; one who forgot completes it after Minchah on Shemini Atzeret.

paragraphs: Belel teshii veyom teshii bechu"l asur leekol velishon bassukka mishshum bal tosip, veen taqqana lipros al hassekak sadin al kullo dahava lah sekak pasul, mishshum dezeh eno nikkar kemo avir vekanaz' bas' bikkure yaaqob, mihu beyom teshii achar sheqqiddesh veakal chutz lassukka, muttar lo leekol batztzahorayim o bemincha betok hassukka shekkebar nikkar dela abar al lo tosip meachar shebballayla vegam bayyom akal chutz lassukka, vela chayeshinan lemarit ayin deorechim shenniknasin lebeto bishat mincha veroin okel bassukka veayyen bikkure yaaqob:

clarification.explanation: On the night of the ninth day and the day of the ninth day (Simchat Torah) in the Diaspora, it is forbidden to eat and sleep in the sukkah, under the law of "you shall not add" (the prohibition against extending the duration of a mitzvah beyond what the Torah fixed). There is no remedy of spreading a sheet over the whole schach, since that would render the schach invalid, as it would no longer be recognizable as being like air, as written in the book Bikurei Yaakov. However, on the ninth day, after he has already made Kiddush and eaten outside the sukkah, he is permitted afterward to eat at midday or at Minchah inside the sukkah — since it is already evident that he does not transgress "you shall not add," seeing that both at night and during the day he ate outside the sukkah. One need not be concerned about the appearance created for guests who enter at the time of Minchah and see him eating in the sukkah.
takeaways: On the night and day of Simchat Torah (the ninth day) in the Diaspora it is forbidden to eat or sleep in the sukkah, on account of 'you shall not add'; there is no remedy of covering the schach with a sheet.
If he already ate his first meal outside the sukkah, he may later that same day eat inside it, since it has already been demonstrated that he is not treating it as an obligatory sukkah.

paragraphs: Hahaqqapot osin bechu"l bsh" vbsh"t veen lachush lechashesha shel haggaon chida" za"l, ki hazzeman nishtanna atta veniptechu enehem shel bene adam vela atu lezilzule, ukepi rabbenu harasha"sh za"l tzarik lehannicha s"t al hatteba veyochazennu adam yere shamayim kol meshek hahahaqqapot, uminhago shel rabbenu haari"y za"l lehaqqip bs"t, gam minhago shel rabbenu haari"y za"l laasot haqqapot lel isru chag achar tepillat arbit, veken rauy laasot kol adam:

clarification.explanation: Hakafot are performed in the Diaspora both on Shemini Atzeret and on Simchat Torah, and one need not be concerned about the concern raised by the Chida, of blessed memory (who worried about disrespect), because times have changed and people today understand and do not come to treat it with disrespect. According to the Rashash, a Torah scroll should be placed on the reader's table, and a God-fearing person should hold it throughout the entire duration of the hakafot. The custom of the Ari, of blessed memory, was to circle while himself holding a Torah scroll, and he also used to perform hakafot on the night of Isru Chag (the day after the festival) after the Arvit prayer — and so it is fitting for every person to do.
takeaways: Hakafot are performed in the Diaspora on both Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah, and it is also recommended to perform additional hakafot on the night of Isru Chag, following the custom of the Ari, of blessed memory.

paragraphs: Mah shemmarbim besimcha likbod hattora hi mitzva gedola, ubekol dabar yekavven haadam leshem shamayim veyizzaher milleareb betok hassimcha shel tora sechoq veqallut rosh ch"v, veita bammidrash vedavid mekarker bekol oz lipne Adonai, mahu bekol oz bekol kocho, mahu mekarker shehaya makkeh yadayv zo al gab zo vetopeach veomer veku', uperesh beor shibat hayyamim shehaya mekavven lehagbir hayyamin al hassemol, vechesed al gebura verachamim al haddin, vehaya mekavven lematteq y"z chamishsha geburot haremuzim bechamesh etzbeot hayyamin, vechamesh peamim chamesh behakkaa hem k"h, siman laddabar koh tebaraku et bene yisrael umikkan semek leminhag yisrael besimchat hattora:

clarification.explanation: Increasing joy in honor of the Torah on Simchat Torah is a great mitzvah, and in every act one should direct his intention toward Heaven, being careful not to mix into the joy of the Torah any levity or frivolity, God forbid. The Midrash brings that King David "danced with all his might before the Lord" — "with all his might" meaning with all his strength, and "mecharker" meaning that he was striking his hands one against the other, clapping, and speaking, etc. The explanation: throughout the seven days of the festival he intended to strengthen the right over the left — that is, chesed over gevurah, mercy over judgment — and through this to sweeten the five gevurot alluded to in the five fingers of the right hand. Five times five in the clapping equals twenty-five, a hint found in the verse "So shall you bless the children of Israel" (koh = 25) — and from this comes support for the Jewish custom on Simchat Torah.
takeaways: The great joy of Simchat Torah must be directed toward Heaven, without levity or frivolity.

Clapping hands on Simchat Torah is grounded (mystically) in King David's practice, by which he sweetened judgment with kindness — five times five, corresponding to the numerical value of 'So shall you bless the children of Israel.'
